variant.name: Customizing Dragons
entries: You can customize any dragon's stat block to reflect the dragon's unique character. Minor changes such as those below are easy to make and have no impact on a dragon's challenge rating.

entries.name: Languages
entries: Most dragons prefer to speak Draconic but learn Common for dealing with allies and minions. But given their high Intelligence and long life span, dragons can easily learn additional languages. You can add languages to a dragon's stat block.

entries.name: Skills
entries: Most dragons are proficient in the {@skill Perception} and {@skill Stealth} skills, and many dragons have additional skill proficiencies. As with languages, you can customize a dragon's skill list (even doubling their proficiency bonus with certain skills) to reflect particular interests and activities. You can also give a dragon tool proficiencies, particularly if the dragon spends time in Humanoid form.

entries.name: Other Traits and Actions
entries: You can borrow traits and actions from other monsters to add unique flavor to a dragon. Consider these examples:

items.name: Change Shape
entries: You can decide that a dragon acquires this action at a younger age than usual, particularly if you want to feature a dragon in Humanoid form in your campaign:

The dragon magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating no higher than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the dragon's choice).

In a new form, the dragon retains its alignment, hit points, Hit Dice, ability to speak, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair actions, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, as well as this action. Its statistics and capabilities are otherwise replaced by those of the new form, except any class features or legendary actions of that form.

entries: You might decide that dragons in your campaign, being an essential part of the Material Plane, are nearly impossible to destroy. A dragon's life essence might be preserved in the egg from which it first emerged, in its hoard, or in a cavernous hall at the center of the world, just as a lich's essence is hidden in a phylactery.

If it has an essence-preserving object, a destroyed dragon gains a new body in {@dice 1d10} days, regaining all its hit points and becoming active again. The new body appears within 5 feet of the object.

items.name: Special Senses

A translucent Greenish scaled dragon with crystal spikes all over the body 4 bigger ones on the tip of the tail, a formation of large crystals along the back spine.

entries.name: Personality
entries: Crystal dragons are artists that like sculping, they like pretty things and shiny things, they spend most of their time seeking beauty. They often do not pull any punches when it comes to creating beautiful sculpures.

entries.name: Society
entries: Crystal dragon societies consist of crystal lizards of any age and very few crystal dragons who serve as leaders, the higher amount of elemental essence the higher their rank is.
These societies are most times near places where elemental crystals grow.
When crystal dragons think they are ready they depart to create their own home.

entries.name: Glittering Hoards
entries: For their treasure hoards, crystal dragons prize diamonds and baubles that refract light, collections of prophecy, works on art of many kinds. When it comes to magical treasure, they seek items and spells that  create or manipulate light or earth, or channel positive energy for healing and nurturing.

entries.name: A Crystal Dragon's Lair
entries: Crystal dragons dwell in underground or mountainous regions, where they construct crystaline structures, corridors, open spaces, caves for lizards and dragons alike, the further and higher these caves are the higher the rank. Glittering crystals scattered about their lairs glow with gathered starlight, and caves or tunnels beneath the earth provide protected areas for their hoards. They use their burrowing ability to dig blinds and secret passages throughout their lairs, allowing them to move easily—and potentially unnoticed.
The challenge rating of a legendary crystal dragon increases by 1 when it's encountered in its lair.

entries.name: Lair Actions
entries: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon can take one of the following lair actions; the dragon can't take the same lair action two rounds in a row:

items.name: Beguiling Whisper
items.entry: The dragon telepathically whispers to one creature within range of the dragon's telepathy. The creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by the dragon until initiative count 20 on the next round. A creature {@condition charmed} in this way obeys to the best of its ability any command the dragon issues that isn't directly harmful to the creature.

items.name: Ice Passage
items.entry: The dragon can open a passage through a wall of ice or snow that is up to 5 feet thick, creating an opening up to 30 feet wide and high.

items.name: Starlight's Gleam
items.entry: The dragon chooses a point it can see in the lair. Gleaming starlight radiates from that point to fill a 10-foot-radius sphere with dim light. Each creature other than the dragon in that area when the light appears must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 13 ({@damage 2d12}) radiant damage and be outlined in the glow. {@action Attack} rolls made against an outlined creature have advantage, and the creature can't hide or benefit from being {@condition invisible}. The starlight and the glow around any creature fades on initiative count 20 on the next round.

entries.name: Regional Effects
entries: The region surrounding a legendary crystal dragon's lair is altered by the dragon's magic, creating one or more of the following effects:

items.name: Clear Skies

items.name: Crystal Profusion
items.entry: Plentiful quartz crystals form in natural stone within 6 miles of the lair, particularly in places where natural light can shine on the crystals.

items.name: Icy Sight

items.name: Positive Energy
items.entry: Any creature that finishes a long rest within 6 miles of the lair regains two additional spent Hit Dice.

items.name: Thriving Wildlife
items.entry: Animal populations flourish within 6 miles of the lair. Ability checks made to forage for food by hunting, fishing, or trapping in that area are made with advantage.

entries: If the dragon dies, the animal population near the lair returns to normal levels over the course of {@dice 1d10} days. The increased Hit Die recovery ends immediately. The existing abundance of quartz crystals remains, but new crystals form at a normal rate.

entries: Energetic spirits from the Elemental Plane of Air, air elementals gather clouds and winds into ever-changing bodies with indistinct limbs and vague features. Beyond their home plane, these elementals might serve magic-users who conjure them, or they might congregate around nexuses of unbridled planar energy, such as wind-scoured mountain peaks or endless storms. In battle, air elementals batter enemies with powerful gusts or transform into whirlwinds to fling away foes.

entries: Sky Dragon wyrmlings have a long, serpentine body covered in pearlescent white scales that shimmer with a pale green tint when they catch the light. Its most striking feature is its three pairs of wings. The first pair is large and feathered, attached at the shoulder blades like a standard dragon. The third pair is positioned further down the spine, giving the dragon a tiered, aerodynamic silhouette. Their sensitivity to air pressure makes them a natural early-warning system for the church.
The more aggressive wyrmlings choose to fly with the knight orders as combat partners, using their breath to clear battlefields or intercept fliers.
A rare few choose to be mounts for the elite. Because they have three sets of wings, the church uses specialized saddles that anchor to the ribcage to avoid blocking any of the wing joints.

That target takes {@dice 2d6} magical slashing damage and is dragged down to the ground with you, causing a similar area effect as when used against a grounded target.

This spell can be cast as a reaction when the caster begins to fall from a great height. The spell is then cast with no target in mind, doubling its effective range and embedding the sword at a grabable ledge; allowing the safe recovery of the caster. However, if this spell is cast with no applicable ledge, you plummet downwards... Rapidly, doubling any fall damage you would've taken.

components.m: GreatSword

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher the magical slashing damage increases by {@dice 1d6} and the range increases by 5ft for each level above 1st.

spell.name: Air Wave
entries: You brandish the weapon used in the spell's casting and make a melee attack with it against one creature within this spell's range. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack's normal effects, except any damage the target takes becomes slashing damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, its range increases by 20 feet and the melee attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} slashing damage to the target on a hit, for each slot level above 1st.

components.m: a melee weapon worth at least 1 sp)

spell.name: Air Step
entries: You place an enchantment upon the feet of a creature you touch, increasing their jumping abilities for the duration. Until the spell ends, the distance the creature can long jump or high jump is doubled. In addition, as a reaction in response to being airborne at any time, the creature can briefly cause clouds to solidify under their feet for the briefest of moments, allowing them to immediately jump as if they were standing on solid ground.

components.m: Two pieces of Cotton

spell.name: Barrage
entries: As part of the action used to cast this spell, you must make a ranged attack with a bow, firing an arrow against one creature within the spell’s range, otherwise the spell fails. This arrow then splits into four additional arrows. On a hit, the target takes the normal damage of the attack.
Hit or miss, choose four creatures within a 20-foot radius of the target to make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d8} piercing damage on a failed save.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the number of targets you can choose increases by 1 for every level above 1st.

components.m: an arrow

spell.name: Blink Slash
entries: Your weapon glows, and it becomes magical for the duration of the spell if it is not already. Choose one creature within range of the spell. You teleport and make a weapon attack against your target. On a hit, you add an additional {@damage 2d6} Slashing Damage. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks and does not count against your movement this turn.

components.m: A Greatsword

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher the weapon damage is increased by {@dice 1d6} and the range is increased by 5ft for each level above 1st.

spell.name: Blue Shield
entries: You create a blue circular, horizontal plane of force, 3 feet in diameter and 1 inch thick, that floats 3 feet above the ground in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within range, or directly under your feet. The disk remains for the duration, and can hold up to 300 pounds. If more weight is placed on it, the spell ends, and everything on the disk falls to the ground.

You can stand on top of it and lean in any direction to cause it to move. It has a movement speed of 35 feet while you are riding it. If you move across a gap of 10 feet or more while riding the blue shield, your falling speed slows to 30 feet per round. You must succeed an Acrobatics check with dc 10 plus half of the distance to the ground divided by 10 to stay on the blue shield or fall off and take half falling damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2th level or higher the size and weight capacity of the blue shield increase. The increase is measured by multiplying the level of the spell slot. This can allow others to ride the shield with you. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or higher, You can use it to fly (surfing through the air)

spell.name: Lightning Breath
entries: Spew lightning from your mouth

You spew lightning from your mouth, each creature with a 15-foot cone must make a dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 3d6} lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
If this is cast into water the cone doubles in size, if used against a creature drenched by water they take an additional {@damage d6} of damage.

components.m: A brach hit by lightning

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell at higher levels it deals extra {@dice 1d6} per level.

spell.name: Conjure Creature
entries: The standard summoning spell. You summon a spirit from another plane to take the form of a creature and appears in unoccupied space that you can see within range. The creature must be a beast of a CR of 1/2 or lower.
The creature is also considered either fey, fiend or celestial, your choice, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when the spell ends.

The summoned creature is friendly to you and your companions. Roll initiative for the summoned creature, it has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you). If you don't issue any commands to it, it defend itself from hostile creatures, but otherwise takes no actions. The DM has the creature's Statistics.

components.m: A small object from the natural habitat of the creature

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell with a higher level spell slot, you can summon a beast of a CR equal to half the level of the spell slot, rounded up.

spell.name: Conjure Spirit Wolf
entries: You summon the fey spirit of a wolf to aid you. The creature appears in an unoccupied space within range. Its statistics are that of a wolf.
You can communicate telepathically with this wolf and it can respond telepathically using any language you know. It retains its memories between summonings.
The wolf is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. The wolf has its own turns, and it rolls its own initiative. The wolf takes verbal commands from you.
If you have more than one wolf, you can command all of them at the same time as long as you issue the same command to each one.
The wolf disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or the spell ends.

components.m: A wolf hair

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you conjure one additional wolf for every slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Create Buildind
entries: This spell creates a simple building that fits entirely within a 10-foot cube within range. Creatures within this area when you cast the spell are harmlessly pushed to the nearest unoccupied space.

The building may be made of wood, stone, brick, or similar structural material, and can be structured and furnished however you wish. This spell can't create food, magic items, mechanical details more complex than hinges and latches, or anything stronger than iron, and any material removed from the building vanishes instantly. After 7 days or when you create another building with this spell, the building crumbles into the ground and vanishes. You can cast this spell again while it is active to maintain the building’s existence for another 7 days.
Casting this spell on the same building once every 7 days for a year makes it permanent.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can increase the size of the cube by 5 feet for each slot level beyond 1st.

spell.name: Demon Skin
entries: You cover your skin with fiendish scales and grow a small set of horns. For the duration, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC and suffer disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks.

spell.name: Delayed Spell
entries: You focus your energy, holding fast and prepare to unleash it in one blast. When this spell ends due to the duration expiring and if you haven't moved since casting this spell then on your next turn if you cast a damaging Evocation spell, with a casting time of one action, increase one of the initial number of damage dice rolled by two. For example, if you cast Scorching Ray as a 2nd level spell, you can roll {@damage 4d6} fire damage once and {@damage 2d6} fire damage twice. To gain this effect, casting the damaging Evocation spell must be the first thing you do on that turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher increase the number of rounds you are {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} by one and increase the number of damage dice rolled by one for each level above 1st.

spell.name: Detect Weapons
entries: For the duration, you sense the presence of manufactured weapons within 30 feet of you. If you sense weapons in this way, you can use your action to determine their location and type (e.g. "shortsword"). This can detect an improvised weapon if it is wielded by a creature intending to use it as such.
The spell can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

spell.name: Earth's Crush
entries: If you are on or under ground level, you can place both your hands on the ground and send a magic pulse to command it to mold itself as two walls and crush your objective. If your objective is a creature, it must make a dexterity saving throw or receive {@damage 3d6} bludgeoning damage and it gets caught up between the walls, losing all its speed until the end of it's next turn, when the spell ends. If the saving throw succeeds, it only receives half the damage and doesn't get caught up.

components.m: Both hands

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2th level or higher, the spells' damage increases by {@dice 1d6}, for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Earthen Pillar
entries: A nonmagical pillar of earth erupts from a surface into existence at a point you choose within range. The pillar has a diameter of 5 feet, a height of up to 15 feet, AC 10, and 20 hit points. The ground where a pillar appears will attain the maximum possible size in the space available even if there isn't enough space normally. Additionally, you can target the ground under a creature if that creature is large or smaller. If the pillar is created under a creature's space, that creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be lifted by the pillar. A willing creature can choose to fail this saving throw.

If the pillar is prevented from reaching its full height because of a ceiling or other obstacles, a creature on a pillar takes {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage and is {@condition restrained} between the pillar and the obstacle. The {@condition restrained} creature can use its action to make a Strength or Dexterity check against your spell save DC. On a success, the creature is no longer {@condition restrained} by the pillar and must either move or fall off the pillar.

When a pillar is reduced to 0 hit points, it crumbles into rubble, which creates an area of difficult terrain within a 5-foot radius. The rubble lasts until cleared. Each 5-foot section takes 1 minute to clear by hand.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can create one additional pillar for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Ganon's Fist
entries: You concentrate destructive energy into a single, supernaturally-powerful punch. Make a melee spell attack against a creature or object you can reach. On a hit, the target takes force damage equal to {@dice 2d12} plus your Strength modifier. A hit target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet directly away from you and knocked {@condition prone}.

The somatic component of this spell is unusually demanding. You can only cast this spell if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your movement speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the force damage increases by {@dice 1d12} and the total distance pushed increases by 5ft for every level above 1st.

spell.name: Wind Blades
entries: You blow air forward, slashing anything in its path. Choose one target within range. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes slashing damage equal to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The wind disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles, torches, and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them. A nonmagical object that isn’t being worn or carried also takes the damage if it’s in the spell’s area.

components.m: a fan made out of feathers worth at least 1 sp

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Air Cannon
entries: Thrusting your open palm forward, you shoot a concentrated force of wind towards a creature you can see within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d8} bludgeoning damage, then it must make a dex saving throw.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage to the target increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Archer's Eye
entries: You grant a ranged attacker the focus it needs to hit a target that is covered, or you obscure a ranged attacker's vision of you. You grant an attacker +2 to hit covered targets. If spoken in reverse you grant half cover to target against ranged attacks.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you speak this Utterance using a slot of 4th level or higher you grant +5 to hit covered targets. If spoken in reverse, using a slot of 4th level or higher you grant a target three-quarter's cover. When you speak this Utterance using a slot of 6th level you grant +10 to hit covered targets. If spoken in reverse, using a slot of 6th level you grant a target total cover. Additionally, for each level above 2nd that this Utterance is spoken at the effect lasts for an additional round to a maximum of 5 rounds.

spell.name: Aspect of the Crucible: Tail
entries: You create a strong tail that sweeps through foes. All creatures within 10ft must succeed a Strength saving throw or take {@damage 3d6} bludgeoning damage and be knocked {@condition prone}. A creature that succeeds the save takes half damage and is not knocked {{@condition prone}.
As part of casting this spell, you can also use your bonus action to charge the spell. When you do so, the damage dice become {@dice d8}'s and the spell reaches out to 15ft.

components.m: Tip of dragon's tail

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d6}, or {@dice 1d8} if charged, for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Ball Lightning
entries: A sphere of pulsating lightning appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within range and lasts for the duration. A creature that comes within 10 feet of the sphere for the first time on a turn must make a Dexterity saving throw, with disadvantage if it is wearing armor made of metal. The creature takes {@damage 2d8} lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

As a bonus action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet in any direction. A solid barrier blocks the sphere's movement, but the sphere can pass through an opening as small as 1 foot in diameter. The sphere sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius.

When you cast this spell, or as an action on a later turn, you can cause the sphere to detonate. This ends the spell and forces each creature within 10 feet of the sphere to make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d8} lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Black Storm
entries: You release a cacophony of negative energy that erupts from a point of your choice within range. Each creature in a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes {@dice 2d6} necrotic and {@damage 2d6} thunder damage and is knocked {@condition prone} on a failed save. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked {@condition prone}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the necrotic damage or the thunder damage (your choice) increases by {@dice 1d6} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Black Flame Empowerment
entries: You envelop your spells in a dark, unnatural flame that insidiously drains the lifeblood of your targets. For the duration, damage-dealing spells you cast are empowered by the following effects:

Unholy Burn: Creatures affected by the main spell’s damage take an additional {@damage d4} necrotic damage at the start of each of their turns for 1 minute. The flames cannot be extinguished by any conventional means and can only be extinguished by magical means.

Maximum Life Reduction: Whenever you deal damage with a spell empowered by Black Flame, you temporarily reduce the target’s maximum life by an amount equal to the necrotic damage dealt (maximum 5 points per turn). This reduction lasts until they complete a long rest.

Energy Conversion: If a creature is killed while under the effects of Black Flame, you can use your reaction to gain temporary hit points equal to the necrotic damage dealt by the spell that caused its death.

components.m: bone dust or a small bone

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher: Unholy burn's damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each higher level. The maximum life reduction per turn increases by 2 points for each higher level.

spell.name: Bone Shield
entries: You create four bones that hover around you, whirling to defend you whenever you are threatened. Each time you are targeted in an attack roll (such as from a weapon attack or a spell attack roll), a bone moves to intercept the attack and is destroyed. If an attack that is blocked is a critical, it instead breaks 2 bones.

components.m: four shards of bone

spell.name: Carian Greatsword
entries: Materializing from the silver ring used in this spell, a magic, large translucent blue greatsword forms on your hand and slashes forwards. All creatures inside the area need to make a Dexterity saving throw, receiving {@damage 2d10} force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a succesful one.

components.m: Needs to be wearing a silver ring

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the greatsword’s damage increases by {@damage 1d10} slashing damage per level. When casted using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you may cast it again as a Bonus Action on the same turn.

spell.name: Carian Piercer
entries: A large, translucent blue longsword appears in your hand and thrusts forth in a line 15 feet long and 5 feet wide in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 2d10} force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

components.m: a silver ring

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Chains of Ice
entries: You create chains of ice which condense around a creature and attempt to pin it to the ground. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. If it fails, it is {@condition restrained} for a number of minutes equal to your Charisma modifier. If the creature was flying, it falls to the ground and is {@condition restrained} there instead, taking falling damage as appropriate. The target can use its action each turn, to make a Strength check against your Rune Power save DC to break free.

spell.name: Cold Flame
entries: You summon a sphere of cold blue fire in the palm of your hand and hurl it at an enemy. Make a ranged spell attack against a target within range. On a hit the target takes {@damage 2d8} cold damage and is engulfed in cold blue flames. At the start of each of its turns until the spell ends the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save the creature takes {@damage 1d8} cold damage and has its movement speed reduced by 10 feet. On a success the spell ends on the creature.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher the blue flames deal an additional {@damage 1d8} cold damage every turn for every slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Conjure Zora
entries: You conjure Zora, a Dire-wolf. Zora is a passive wolf, who will refuse to attack, but will allow his summoner to ride him. Zora has the same statistics as a standard Dire-wolf. When summoned he appears with a saddle capable of carrying 2 people, an oil lantern, and 2 wolf pups, who travel along with Zora, acting as scouts to warn of danger ahead.

spell.name: Conjure Twin Foxes
entries: You summon spirits of 2 passive foxes to aid you.
The twin foxes appear in an unoccupied space within range. Their statistics are that of a cat though they are celestial, fey, or fiend (your choice) instead of beast, and have an intelligence of 10.

The Foxes are friendly (if a bit sarcastic) to you and your companions. While within 40 feet, they can communicate with you or each other telepathically. The Foxes are unnaturally stealthy able to cast the spell invisibility on themselves, and can be used to scout. However if engaged in combat the foxes will refuse to fight instead taking the dash action to flee.

The Foxes disappear when not in range to communicate with you for more than 1 hour, they drop to 0 hit points, or you re-cast this spell. Although they retain their memories between summonings they drop anything they are holding when they disappear.

spell.name: Dazzling Glare
entries: You unleash an overwhelming flash of light. Choose any number of creatures within range. Each target that can see you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition blinded} for 1 minute; a creature sensitive to sunlight makes this saving throw with disadvantage. If a target is {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating}, its {@status Concentration|XPHB} is also broken on a failed save. A {@condition blinded} target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

spell.name: Earth Hammer
entries: A layer of pebbles and small stones covers the hammer that you hold, which you also use as a weapon. For the duration the weapon's damage die increases by two steps (ex: {@dice 1d4} to {@dice 1d8} to {@dice 1d12} to {@dice 2d8} or {@dice 1d6} to {@dice 1d10} to {@dice 2d6} to {@dice 2d6 + 2}) and it deals an additional {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage on hit.

components.m: Any Hammer

spell.name: Fire Dragon's Wings
entries: You create wings of flame and sweep two nearby enemies. Choose two targets within range. The targets must make a Dexterity saving throw, or take {@damage 1d10} fire damage on a hit. You gain a flying speed of 15ft; you fall if you end your turn in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the fire damage increases by {@dice 1d10} and its duration increases for 1 round for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Hydra Heads
entries: You conjure three hydra heads in three unoccupied spaces within range. Each head must be summoned on the ground, occupies a 5-foot cube and breathes a poisonous cloud in a 15-foot cone from its mouth in a direction of your choice. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 1d8} poison damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. A creature in the area of more than one poisonous cloud is affected only once.
The hydra heads disappear after making their breath attack.

components.m: a vial of hydra bloo

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When casting this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you summon one additional hydra head for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Hyper Voice
entries: You let loose a horribly echoing shout to all creatures within range. All hostile creatures within range must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 3d8} thunder damage and {@damage 3d8} Psychic damage, or half as much on a success. Additionally, if the caster is under the effects of the thaumaturgy spell, or any other spell or feature which makes their voice louder, increase the size of the damage die to {@dice 3d10} instead of {@dice 3d8} for both the thunder and Psychic damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: For every tier above 2nd, increase the Thunder and Psychic damage by {@dice 1d8} and increased its range by an additional 5ft.

spell.name: Booming Word
entries: You utter a divine word that booms with the true voice of gods, audible from up to a mile away. All creatures other than you within a 120-foot radius sphere centered on yourself must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 8d4} thunder damage and becoming {@condition deafened} for one minute on a failed save, or taking half as much damage on a success. The area of effect spreads around corners.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you may choose any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by the spell.

spell.name: Bonesword
entries: A bone, held in your free hand, becomes a shortsword, longsword, greatsword, battleaxe, or greataxe. It lasts for the duration and then reverts to a normal bone. If this spell is cast on the same bone within 24 hours, upon the spell's end it will crumble to dust. Anyone may use the sword, and it is a magic weapon. On a hit, it deals an extra {@damage 2d6} damage against living creatures and an extra {@damage 1d6} damage against good-aligned creatures. The extra damage is of the same type as the weapon's base damage (piercing or slashing).

You may cast this spell on another bone in your other hand (or hands, if it applies) using your bonus action. If using the variant spell points rule, you must use 1 magic point per bone in addition to using your bonus action. All bones will transform back upon the spell's end, and will be destroyed of the spell is used on them again.

components.m: one bone at least 6 inches long

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th or higher, the extra damage inflicted on living creatures increases by {@damage 2d6} and damage inflicted on good-aligned creatures increases by {@dice 1d6} for each two slot levels above 3rd.

spell.name: Conjure Bladestorm
entries: You animate up to three nonmagical swords within range. Each sword begins to hover in the air and becomes a Flying Sword, and it gains a bonus to its attack and damage rolls equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. The flying swords' weapons attacks are magical. The flying sword does the damage die of the base weapon in place of the damage die of the flying sword's longsword attack.

The animated swords are friendly to you and your companions. Roll initiative for the animated swords as a group, which has its own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you). If you don't issue any commands to them, they defend themselves from hostile creatures, but otherwise take no actions. Once given an order, the animated swords continue to follow it until their task is complete.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th or 6th level, you can animate up to six swords. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th or 8th level, you can animate up to nine swords. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, you can animate up to twelve swords.

spell.name: Flame Jump
entries: Bursts of flame fly from under your feet launching you quite far. On your turn as a bonus action you can click your heels together and send fire shooting from your feet. The blast propels you 20 feet in a direction of your choice.
Each creature within 5 feet of you during the initial blast must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 3d6} fire damage.
Until the spell ends, your steps leave charred prints along the ground.

components.m: a pair of boots

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Ice Spear
entries: A frozen spear of ice pierces through a line 30 feet long by 5 feet wide starting at a point in range that you can see. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 6d8} cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

components.m: a vial of water, handfull of snow, or small ice cube

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each slot above 3rd.

spell.name: Lightning Spear
entries: You create a bolt of lightning in your hand, similar in shape to a spear and hurl it at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 6d10} lightning damage, and is {@condition stunned} until the start of its next turn.
This spell deals double damage to dragons and Dragon-type creatures.

components.m: a twig from a tree hit by lightning

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for every slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Lightning Cloak
entries: You coat yourself in yellow lightning, which sparks off of you like an aura of pure electricity. You double your movement speed, gain one extra reaction(which you can only use to parry or make an attack of opportunity) and have advantage on dexterity saving throws for the duration of the spell. Additionally, if a creature within 10 feet of you damages you with an attack or targets you with a harmful spell, that creature takes {@damage 3d8} lightning damage, and is immune to this property of the spell until the beginning of its next turn. During the duration of the spell, you cannot cast any other spells, and when the spell ends, you must succeed on a constitution saving throw against your own spell save dc or gain a level of {@condition exhaustion}.

spell.name: Summon Anthill
entries: Choose an unoccupied space of dirt, soil, or sand within range. With a rumble underfoot, an anthill appears in the chosen space, followed by a swarm of ants.[1] The summoned ants are friendly to you and your companions, and they take their turn(s) immediately after yours. You can issue commands to them telepathically during the spell's duration, which they follow. If you don’t issue any commands to them, they take no actions, even to defend themselves. When the spell ends, any remaining ants return home.
For the duration of the spell, you can use a bonus action to cause a new swarm of ants to appear from the anthill's space if there are no other swarms remaining.

components.m: an antenna

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you summon one additional swarm of ants during the initial casting for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Wall of Vines
entries: You create a wall of vines on a solid surface within range. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick.
The wall is opaque and lasts for the duration.
Each 5-foot square of wall may support up to 50 pounds and has 2 hit points per inch of thickness.

The uneven surface is considered difficult terrain, and climbing it requires succeeding at a Strength (Athletics) check. If a section of wall is reduced to 0 hit points, or exceeds its support weight, that section of wall is considered breached.

The vines also attempt to entangle nearby foes. Any enemies who come in contact with the wall must make a Dexterity saving throw versus your spell save DC or be entangled. They may make a new Dexterity or Strength saving throw to end the entanglement at the end of their turn each round.

components.m: a tendril of ivy

spell.name: Wizard's Tower
entries: You conjure a two-story tower made of stone, wood, or similar suitably sturdy materials. The tower can be round or square in shape. Each level of the tower is 10 feet tall and has an area of up to 200 square feet. Access between levels can consist of a simple ladder and hatch or an arrangement of stairs. Each level takes one of the following forms, chosen by you when you cast the spell:
A personal bedroom with a bed, chairs, chest, and magical fireplace
A barrack style bedroom with 8 beds in 4 bunks, an equal number of lockers, and a central round table and chairs
A study with desks, books, bookshelves, parchments, ink, and ink pens
A library able to magically preserve stored books and others forms of written works
A kitchen space with ovens, magical burner hobs, cooking utensils, a pantry, refrigerator, and freezer to store food
A dining space with a table, chairs, eating utensils, ceramics and glass finery
A lounge with couches, armchairs, side tables and footstools
A washroom with toilets, washtubs, a magical brazier, and sauna benches
A blacksmiths forge with furnace, tools and grindstones
An observatory with a telescope and maps of the night sky
An unfurnished, empty room

The interior of the tower is warm and dry, regardless of conditions outside. Any equipment or furnishings conjured with the tower dissipate into smoke if removed from it. At the end of the spell’s duration, all creatures and objects within the tower that were not created by the spell appear safely outside on the ground, and all traces of the tower and its furnishings disappear.

The tower and any of the many rooms its contains can be locked down placing the room, floor or tower entire under a ‘Forbiddance’ preventing all forms of intrusion below the towers own spell slot level. The caster and anyone they appoint retains the ability to lock and unlock the tower, alternatively a key device can be created to serve this function.

components.m: a fragment of stone, wood, and all other building materials that are to be used in the tower

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the tower can have one additional story for each slot level beyond 3rd.

spell.name: Black Arrow
entries: For the duration, any time you hit with a ranged weapon attack, you deal an extra {@damage 2d8} necrotic damage. If this attack reduces a Medium or Small humanoid to 0 hit points, the humanoid must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or immediately be raised as skeleton, as if you had cast animate dead.

spell.name: Bolts of Tiamat
entries: You create five glowing bolts of energy, each a different color. One glows an icy blue, one a fiery red, one a crackling yellow, one an acidic green, and one a poisonous purple.

Each hits a creature of your choice that you can see within range. Each bolt has a different damage type, dealing {@damage 1d10 + 5} damage from its respective type (cold, fire, lightning, poison, acid) to its target. The bolts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one target or several.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher you may increase one bolt's damage by {@dice 1d10} for each level above 4th.

spell.name: Creation of Wings
entries: You gain {@dice 3d10} Temporary hit points in the form of two iridescent, insectoid wings. While you have these Temporary Hitpoints, you have a Fly speed of 30 feet.

components.m: A wax figure of a vulture

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot above 4th you gain 1 extra {@dice d10} Temporary hitpoints for every slot above 4th.

spell.name: Lightning Leap
entries: You let loose a line of lightning that is 60 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 5d10} lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. You can then teleport to an unoccupied space touched by the line.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this at a 5th level or higher, you deal an additional {@dice 1d10} per slot above 4th.

spell.name: Conjure Skeletons
entries: You choose 4 piles of bones, of which you can use to summon Skeletons. You can use this in any combination.
You can Choose 1 pile to create 4 CR1 Skeletons, 2 piles to create 2 CR2 Skeletons or 3 piles to Create a CR3.
The Skeletons disappear when they drop to 0 hit points or when the spell ends.

The Skeletons are friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Roll initiative for the Skeletons as a group, which has its own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you).

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: At higher Levels you can Choose one extra pile per slot used above 5th.

spell.name: Advanced apraisal
entries: After casting this spell on a target you can see more complete information about the target.
You know its race, challenge rate level and basic attributes.

spell.name: Perfect Identification
entries: After casting this spell the caster must make an ability check equal to the target CR level and if the caster suceeds they can see the complete information about the target.

spell.name: Energy Dispel
entries: When casting this spell choose a target that is made of energy, if its not alive and a spell of lower level you can dispel it. if its higher level spell or its comes from other creature roll a dice with the modifier of the ability used to cast this spell dc the level of the spell +10 or the cr of the creature.

spell.name: Magic Arrows
entries: You Utter the incantation as you put your hands together fingers interlocked creating three glowing arrows of magical force on top of you, when your hands lock together the arrows shoot. Each arrow hits a creature of your choice that you can see within range. A dart deals {@damage 1d8 + 2} force damage to its target. The arrows all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the spell creates one more dart for each slot level above 3st.

spell.name: Apraisal
entries: After casting this spell on a target you can see information about the target.
You know its race, and two random basic attributes.

spell.name: Angel Arrow
entries: You firmly grab your bow and get into shooting position, then you put your hands in, has if there as an arrow in the bow that you can grab, as you start to pull energy starts forming in the shape of an arrow, and as you release it, red energy resembling an arrow with a fiery spiral of flames shoots in the direction you aimed at.
Make a ranged attack roll against one creature within 5 feet of you. On a hit, the arrow hits its mark, causing a small explosion dealing {@damage 1d6} radiant damage to the target.

components.m: A bow, a crossbow, something that shoot arrows or stuff that resembles it

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: This spell’s damage increases by {@dice 1d6} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d6}), 11th level ({@dice 3d6}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d6}).

spell.name: Arcane Arrow
entries: You imbue your ranged weapon with arcane energy, causing it to crackle at the seams with power. The next time you successfully hit a ranged weapon attack with it before the spell's duration ends, the projectile explodes violently. Every creature within 5 feet of the target, including the target itself, must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d6} force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
Make a ranged attack roll against one creature within 5 feet of you. On a hit, the arrow hits its mark, causing a small explosion dealing {@damage 1d6} radiant damage to the target.

components.m: a weapon worth at least 1 sp with the Range property

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 2d6} for every level above 1st.

spell.name: Booming Arrow

m.text: a ranged weapon worth at least 1 sp

entries: You brandish the weapon used in the spell's casting and make a ranged attack with it against one creature. The target suffers the weapon attack's normal effects and is sheathed in booming energy. For each 5 feet the target moves, it makes a booming beat from within it and takes {@damage 1d8} thunder damage.

races.name: Half-Elf (Variant; Moon Elf or Sun Elf Descent)

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: This spell's damage increases when you reach certain levels. At 5th level, the ranged attack deals an extra {@damage 1d8} thunder damage to the target on a hit, and the damage the target takes for moving increases to {@dice 2d8}. Both damage rolls increase by {@dice 1d8} at 11th level ({@dice 2d8} and {@dice 3d8}) and again at 17th level ({@dice 3d8} and {@dice 4d8}).

spell.name: Violent Elemental Arrow

components.m: a bow worth at least 1 sp

entries: With one hand on bow you utter the incantation slowly as you draw an imaginary arrow from your bow. As you draw the arrow the energy from the arrow violently moves around giving disadvantage on projectile attacks against you as a colored sharp and slightly unstable energy arrow is draw. The appearance of this arrow's energy is determined by what element you choose.
As you let go of the arrow the bow strings are audible heard 20 ft around you dealing {@damage 6d8} of your chosen element damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@scaledamage 6d8|3-9|1d8} for each slot level above 3rd.
asdasdasdasdasda.

item.item: A signet ring of your noble house

entries: {@b Skill proficiencies:} Nature, Survival
{@b Tool proficiencies:} Smith, Weaver
{@b Equipment:} A signet ring of your noble house, Hooded Elegant lake-green robes, 15 gold.

Born into one of the oldest lineages of the lake elves, you carry the weight of centuries of tradition. Your family has long guarded the sacred waters, mediating disputes between the fey, elves, and the mortal realm. Even the ripples of the lake seem to acknowledge your presence, as if recognizing the blood that courses through your veins.

The waters of your homeland are more than just lakes and rivers, they are conduits of magic, and through them, you feel the whispers of spirits, the guidance of ancestors, and the ebb and flow of power older than most civilizations. Your people know that a scion of your house can commune with the lake itself, drawing insight and subtle influence from its depths.

From an early age, you were trained in diplomacy, etiquette, and the arcane lore of water and fey. Your days were filled with lessons in language, ritual, and lore, preparing you to stand among nobles and rulers. While many scions inherit wealth or land, you inherited knowledge, subtlety, and the responsibility to maintain your family’s legacy.

Perhaps your family once mediated a dispute that shaped the course of the surrounding realm. Perhaps a lake spirit bound to your lineage seeks your aid. Perhaps a rival house questions your right to the ancestral title. Your story is tied to water, magic, and the weight of a noble legacy that few can claim.

entries.name: Heir of the Lake
entries: You are recognized among Lake Elf communities as a member of a noble or mystical lineage. You gain advantage on Charisma checks when interacting with other elves and fey creatures, and you know secret lore about your family’s lands and ancestral magic. You can call upon minor favors or knowledge from allies tied to your lineage.

entries.name: Noble Fey etiquette
entries: Born into one of the ancient lineages of the lake elves, you are a scion of prestige and power. Your upbringing was surrounded by the mystic waters, and your family’s influence extends across the shores of your homeland. You are trained in etiquette, arcane knowledge, and the subtle ways of politics and diplomacy among elves and fey alike.

entries.name: Mistical Lake Secrets
entries: Once per long rest, you can cast Misty Step but only when you are within 30 ft of natural water source(lake, river, stream).
You can see through fog, mist, or obscured water up to 30 feet as if it were clear.
Once per long rest, you can move across water as if it were solid terrain for up to 30 ft, leaving a shimmering ripple in your wake.

entries.name: Mistical Lake Connection
entries: You have a slight connection to the mistical lake as you were raised and grew basically on it, when you rest in water you regain extra 1 hitpoint per hitdie spent, and one hitpoint regarless.

If you stay in a body of water pound sized or smaller for too long, it starts forming a small conection to the mistical lake, it begins transforming into an extension of the lake, it gains the following properties:
>Staying submerged in the lake for one day cures any nonmagical disease;
>By Staying submerged for 1 month, it cures normal curses and magical curses up to 2nd level;
>Undead Creatures of CR 3 or lower cant get within 30ft of the lake as it repels them;

feat.name: Healer Revised
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Battle Medic
entries: If you have a Healer's Kit, you can expend one use of it and tend to a creature within 5 feet of yourself as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action. That creature can expend one of its Hit Point Dice, and you then roll that die. The creature regains a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Healing Rerolls
entries: Whenever you roll a die to determine the number of Hit Points you restore with a spell or with this feat's Battle Medic benefit, you can reroll the die if it rolls a 1, and you must use the new roll.

entries.name: First Aid
entries: You learn the First Aid Spell, this spell lets you provide first aid to a creature

entries.name: Ability score increase.
entries: Your Dexterity score increases by 2 and either your constitution or charisma increasses by 1.

entries.name: Age
entries: Although elves reach physical maturity at about the same age as humans, the elven understanding of adulthood goes beyond physical growth to encompass worldly experience. An elf typically claims adulthood and an adult name around the age of 100 and can live to be 950 years old.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Lake elves tend toward neutral alignments.

entries.name: Size
entries: Lake elves range from under 5 to over 7 feet tall and have slender builds. Your size is Medium.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 30 feet and you have 30ft swiming speed.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: Accustomed to twilit forests, moonlit shores, and the dim depths of lakes, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry.
entries: You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the charmed condition on yourself and you can survive up to one week without water of food.

entries.name: Child of the lake
entries: You can breathe air and water, and you have resistance to cold damage. You can also hold your breath for one hour.

entries.name: Trance
entries: Elves do not sleep. Instead they meditate deeply, remaining semi-conscious, for 4 hours a day. The Common word for this meditation is trance. While meditating, you dream after a fashion; such dreams are actually mental exercises that have become reflexive after years of practice. After resting in this way, you gain the same benefit a human would from 8 hours of sleep.

entries.name: Keen senses
entries: You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

entries.name: Lake Elf Training.
entries: You have proficiency with polearms and net.

entries.name: Lake senses
entries: You have 10 feet of tremorsense.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, aquan and Elven.
asdasdasdasdasda.

lairActions: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon can take one of the following lair actions; the dragon can't take the same lair action two rounds in a row:

items.name: Beguiling Whisper
items.entry: The dragon telepathically whispers to one creature within range of the dragon's telepathy. The creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by the dragon until initiative count 20 on the next round. A creature {@condition charmed} in this way obeys to the best of its ability any command the dragon issues that isn't directly harmful to the creature.

items.name: Earth Passage
items.entry: The dragon can open a passage through a wall of Dir, Stone or minerals that is up to 5 feet thick, creating an opening up to 30 feet wide and high.

items.name: Starlight's Gleam
items.entry: The dragon chooses a point it can see in the lair. Gleaming starlight radiates from that point to fill a 10-foot-radius sphere with dim light. Each creature other than the dragon in that area when the light appears must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 13 ({@damage 2d12}) radiant damage and be outlined in the glow. {@action Attack} rolls made against an outlined creature have advantage, and the creature can't hide or benefit from being {@condition invisible}. The starlight and the glow around any creature fades on initiative count 20 on the next round.

regionalEffects: The region surrounding a legendary crystal dragon's lair is altered by the dragon's magic, creating one or more of the following effects:

items.name: Clear Skies
items.entry: The skies above a crystal dragon's lair remain clear and free of precipitation unless magically altered. Winds blow lightly, posing little threat to those approaching the lair, and visibility is the best possible for the time of day.

items.name: Crystal Profusion
items.entry: Plentiful quartz crystals form in natural stone within 6 miles of the lair, particularly in places where natural light can shine on the crystals.

items.name: Icy Sight
items.entry: Ice and quartz within 6 miles of the lair become conduits for the dragon's psionic presence. As an action, the dragon can cast the {@spell clairvoyance} spell, requiring no spell components and targeting any ice or quartz crystals in that region.

items.name: Positive Energy
items.entry: Any creature that finishes a long rest within 6 miles of the lair regains two additional spent Hit Dice.

items.name: Thriving Wildlife
items.entry: Animal populations flourish within 6 miles of the lair. Ability checks made to forage for food by hunting, fishing, or trapping in that area are made with advantage.

regionalEffects: If the dragon dies, the animal population near the lair returns to normal levels over the course of {@dice 1d10} days. The increased Hit Die recovery ends immediately. The existing abundance of quartz crystals remains, but new crystals form at a normal rate.

lairActions: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon can take one of the following lair actions; the dragon can't take the same lair action two rounds in a row:

items.name: Aero-Projection:
items.entry: The dragon chooses a point it is aware of within 5 miles. It creates a small, swirling vortex of wind at that location. For 1 minute, the dragon can see and hear through that vortex as if it were standing there. Additionally, it can speak through the vortex, its voice sounding like a whistling breeze.

items.name: Buffeting Gale:
items.entry: A localized hurricane-force wind kicks up in a 60-foot radius around a point the dragon can see. Each creature in that area must succeed on a {@dc 17} Strength saving throw or be pushed 40 feet away from the center and knocked prone.

items.name: Aural Resonance
items.entry: The dragon causes the wind to whistle through its hoard of bells and chimes. Every creature of the dragon's choice within 60 feet must succeed on a {@dc 18} Wisdom saving throw or be Charmed or Frightened (dragon's choice) until the end of their next turn.

items.name: Wind-borne Secrets:
items.entry: Within 10 miles of the lair, the wind carries conversations to the dragon. If a creature speaks a secret or a plan out loud while outdoors, there is a chance the dragon hears it perfectly. This makes the territory around the Church's temples impossible to infiltrate by traditional means; the very air the intruders breathe betrays them to the guardian.

items.name: Low Pressure Zone
items.entry: The dragon thins the air in a 20-foot radius sphere. Creatures in the area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain one level of exhaustion that lasts until they finish a short rest.

items.name: Crystal spikes
items.entry: The dragon Chooses a point in its lair 10ft by 10 and crystal spikes start growing and shooting from it. It shoots 4 different waves. Each wave can target a different creature. Targeted creatures must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity Saving throw or take 4d4 Magical Piercing dmg per wave.

regionalEffects: The region surrounding a legendary crystal dragon's lair is altered by the dragon's magic, creating one or more of the following effects:

items.name: The Unbroken Gale
items.entry: Within 10 miles of the dragon’s lair, the wind never stops. It is a constant, howling force that shapes the entire ecosystem. The entire region is under the effects of Strong Wind.

Within 1 mile of the lair, the winds become Violent. Any creature flying in this area that isn't a Sky Dragon or a chosen Knight of the Church must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength (Athletics) check at the start of each turn or be blown 20 feet in a random direction and lose their flying speed until the start of their next turn.

The wind whistles through the mountain cracks and church spires in a way that mimics speech. The dragon can whisper into the wind at the center of its lair, and the wind will carry that exact message to any point within the 10-mile radius, allowing it to speak to pilgrims or warn intruders.

items.name: Weightless Winds
items.entry: Within 1 mile of the lair, gravity feels slightly weaker. Jumping distances are doubled, and falling damage is halved as the wind naturally pushes upward to catch anything that falls.

items.name: Atmospheric Attunement
items.entry: A Sky Dragon can see through any air current that originates from or passes through its lair. This works like a massive, invisible web. The dragon can sense the heartbeat, breathing, and movement of any creature touching the air within a certain radius (usually miles for an adult). Because the wind is everywhere, it’s almost impossible to hide from them unless you are in a vacuum or a completely airtight lead box.

items.name: Wind-borne Secrets
items.entry: Within 10 miles of the lair, the wind carries conversations to the dragon. If a creature speaks a secret or a plan out loud while outdoors, there is a chance the dragon hears it perfectly. This makes the territory around the Church's temples impossible to infiltrate by traditional means; the very air the intruders breathe betrays them to the guardian.

items.name: The Singing Peaks
items.entry: The wind constantly plays through the rock formations and temple architecture, creating a low, melodic humming. This sound calms domestic animals and makes it impossible for creatures to be surprised by non-magical means, as the wind carries the sound of footsteps perfectly.

regionalEffects.name: Lair Traits: The Horde
regionalEffects.entry: A Sky Dragon’s lair doesn't have piles of gold. Instead, it features:

regionalEffects: The Wind-Chime Forest: Thousands of bells and metal rods hanging from the ceiling or jagged rocks.
The Ribbon Spires: Long, enchanted silk banners that never fray, used to track the complex "currents" the dragon uses for sleep-flying.
Vibration Pools: Shallow basins of water that perfectly mirror the vibrations of the atmosphere, allowing the dragon to "see" weather patterns days in advance.
If the dragon dies, these effects fade over {1d10} days, and the air becomes heavy and stagnant.

classFeature.name: Martial Strikes
entries: Beginning at 1st level when you make an unarmed attack you can choose to use either your Strength or your dexterity, and the damage of those strikes becomes 1d4+ your str or dex modifier.
At level 5 the dice becomes 1d6 instead.
At level 10 the dice becomes 1d8 instead.
At level 15 the dice becomes 1d10 instead.
At level 18 the dice becomes 1d12 instead.
Before you make a melee attack, you can choose to take a -2 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +4 to the attack's damage.
You are proficient in the martial skill.

classFeature.name: Martial Strike
entries: Before you make a melee attack, you can choose to take a -2 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +4 to the attack's damage.

classFeature.name: Unarmored defense
entries: At 1st level while you are not wearing any armor, your armor class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Strength or Constituion modifier.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Movement
entries: Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.
At level 5 the movement bonus becomes 15ft instead.
At level 10 the movement bonus becomes 20ft instead.
At level 15 the movement bonus becomes 25ft instead.
At level 18 the movement bonus becomes 30ft instead.

classFeature.name: Deflect Projectile
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you are attacked by a projectile you can use your reaction to add +2 to your ac potentially making the attack to fail by catching it and deflecting it against a creature within 30ft + half your proficiency modifier number worth of 5t squares.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Martial Sense
entries: With experience comes wisdom. So they say, but what you got from experience is different.
At 7th level you are so experienced in fighting that you can do it with your eyes closed, you gain 20ft of blind sense and 10ft of tremor sense.
If a creature is within 10ft of you and its not flying, that creature cannot attack you at advantage, and you cannot attack it with disadvantage.

classFeature.name: Movement Dertemination
entries: At lvl 10, you are so determinated to fight that nothing can block your way.
If you move throught difficult terrain that restricts your movements, you ignore half of that restriction, if you need to use 20ft of movement to move 5ft, you instead only need 10ft.
You ignore the effects of difficult terrain, for example in spike growth you ignore the damage.
You gain a Swim and climbing speed equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier times 5.
You completly ignore movement restrictions of difficult terrain at lvl 15.

classFeature.name: Expert Level
entries: At level 14th you´ve had your fair share of fighting, by now you have accumulated a fair share of experience and your fighting style shows it.
You have proficiency in all saving throws.
When you fail saving throw, once per day you can choose to succeed instead.
You have expertise on the martial skill.
Once per round when you hit a attack roll you can make the target make a Dexterity saving throw (DC= 8+PB+STR/DEX), on a fail they are knocked prone.

classFeature.name: Martial Artist Strength
entries: At lvl 18, you are so experienced in fighting and your body is at its peak that you become a force to be reckoned with.

Your senses are upgraded, you gain extra 15ft of blind sense and 10ft of tremor sense. Any creature within 20ft of cannot attack you at advantage and you cannot attack it at disadvantage, additionally attack rolls you make against these creatures have a +2 bonus and attacks rolls they make against you have a -2 bonus.

classFeature.name: Favored TARGET
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.

Choose a type of favored target: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.

When you make an attack roll against your favored target you can add half your PB rounded up to result. Additionally when you deal damage to your favored target you can add half your PB rounded up to the result.
From Level 6 you cant have disadvantage on attack rolls against your favored Target.
From Level 14 When you make your favored target make a saving throw, they make it at disadvantage.
When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all.

You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.

classFeature.name: Natural Explorer
entries: Also at 1st level, you are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or the Underdark. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you’re proficient in.

entries.name: While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:
entries: Difficult terrain doesn’t slow your group’s travel.
Your group can’t become lost except by magical means.
Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.
At level 3 you cant be surprised while you are in your favorite terrain.
At level 6 you can additionally add your PB to all skill checks you make while in your fav terrain.
At lvl 12 you cant suffer from disadvantage while in your favorite terrain. Other creatures cant gain advantage on  attack rolls against you while you are in your favorite terrain.
You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

classFeature.name: Tracking Arrow
entries: Using a bonus action you choose a creature you can see within range of your ranged weapon and create a magic arrow that you shoot at the target. This arrow last's for 1 minute or until you dismiss it.
While a creature is affected by this arrow you always vaguely know its location within 100ft. Additionally if its your favored target you always know its precise location.
When you make a attack against the target you can add half your PB rounded down. If the target is your favored target add your PB.

When you deal damage to the creature affected by this arrow you deal an additional d4. This damage increases to 1d6 at level 5, 1d8 at level 10, 1d10 at level 15 and 1d12 at level 18. Additionally if the target is your favorite target add half your PB rounded down.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
Archery. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Blind Fighting. You have blind sight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.
Defense. While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Druidic Warrior. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. They count as ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip from the Druid spell list.
Dueling. When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Thrown Weapon Fighting. You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon. In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.
Two-Weapon Fighting. When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

Close Quarters Shooter (UA). When making a ranged attack while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have disadvantage on the attack roll. Your ranged attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover against targets within 30 feet of you. You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls on ranged attacks.

Interception (UA). When a creature you can see hits a target that is within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage the target takes by 1d10 + your proficiency bonus (to a minimum of 0 damage). You must be wielding a shield or a simple or martial weapon to use this reaction.
Mariner (UA). As long as you are not wearing heavy armor or using a shield, you have a swimming speed and a climbing speed equal to your normal speed, and you gain a +1 bonus to armor class.

Tunnel Fighter (UA). As a bonus action, you can enter a defensive stance that lasts until the start of your next turn. While in your defensive stance, you can make opportunity attacks without using your reaction, and you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against a creature that moves more than 5 feet while within your

Unarmed Fighting (UA). Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier. If you strike with two free hands, the d6 becomes a d8. When you successfully start a grapple, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to the grappled creature. Until the grapple ends, you can also deal this damage to the creature whenever you hit it with a melee attack.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does.

entries.name: Mana Points:
entries: The Ranger table shows how many manapoints you have to cast your ranger spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a mana points of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher:
entries: You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the ranger spell list.

The Spells Known column of the Ranger table shows when you learn more ranger spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 5th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the ranger spells you know and replace it with another spell from the ranger spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability:
entries: Difficult terrain doesn’t slow your group’s travel.

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your ranger spells, since your magic draws on your attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a ranger spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier}
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier}

At 2nd level, you can use a druidic focus as a spellcasting focus for your ranger spells. A druidic focus might be a sprig of mistletoe or holly, a wand or rod made of yew or another special wood, a staff drawn whole from a living tree, or an object incorporating feathers, fur, bones, and teeth from sacred animals.

classFeature.name: Primeval Awareness
entries: Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action and expend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the spell slot you expend, you can sense whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or within up to 6 miles if you are in your favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. This feature doesn’t reveal the creatures’ location or number.
