classFeature.name: Land's Stride
entries: Starting at 8th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such as those created by the Entangle spell.

classFeature.name: Hide in Plain Sight
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other naturally occurring materials with which to create your camouflage.

Once you are camouflaged in this way, you can try to hide by pressing yourself up against a solid surface, such as a tree or wall, that is at least as tall and wide as you are. You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions. Once you move or take an action or a reaction, you must camouflage yourself again to gain this benefit.

classFeature.name: Vanish
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

classFeature.name: Feral Senses
entries: At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.
You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, you aren't blinded or deafened.

classFeature.name: Foe Slayer
entries: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored Target. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.

entries: There are various types of dimension pockets that one can be born with, every type has its own qualities and effects.Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

classFeature.name: Dimensional Contract
entries: Think on how you are gonna make the creature do the contract with you, you can make their wish come true, fix the lingering worries of an undead, mayhaps some creature wants to see the world, some might help you if you give them tasty treats every time you summon them, or perphaps some creature will accept the shelter and food you offer them.

You can make a contract with a willing creature that your dimensional pocket has space for(check the Dimension Pocket table), more than one creature can be stored as long as the cr of the creatures combined doesnt exceed the space. You can demisse contract at any time, thought most summoners leave their ex summons at a summoner school.
If you make a contract with a creature that was made by the effect of a spell or likes, the spell ends, if the spell had a duration, the creature stays until you dimiss the contract.
Creatures in the summoning space dont go hungry as they consume the magic of your dimension pocket.

Creatures inside the Dimension Pocket heal for 4hp every hour(the hp increasse's as you lvl up check tabble), ailments(like curses or other status effects) disperse while the creature is on the dimension pocket, a weaker ailment normally disperses within 24hours, the stronger the ailment the longer it takes for it to cure.
When a creature you made a contract with reach's 0 hit points they faint, and basically act the same as a player when they do so.

classFeature.name: Pocket Dimension Summoning
entries: You can use your action to summon one creature inside your pocket Space to a place you can see within 5ft, you can also use an action or bonus action to dismiss a summon.
You can use your action to enter and exit your Pocket Space, when you exit you go back to the same place you were before.

The distance you can summon a creature to increases to 10ft when you reach 3rd level in this class, 20ft when you reach 6th level in this class, 25ft when you reach 9th level in this class, 35ft when you reach 12th level in this class, 40ft when you reach 16th level in this class and 50ft when you reach 19th level in this class.

You have a lot of Mana Due to the magic inside you but you can cast spells of 6th level and higher due to having a dimension inside of you, if you cast spells of 6th or higher levels the dimension is at risk of collapsing, If it collapses you Explode with 50ft radius dealing 20d12's fire damage per Summoner level after 9th.

classFeature.name: Magic Injection
entries: Starting at 5th Level your pocket dimension is big enough so you can take out most of its magic outside in one swoop and enchant one creature.
You can use your action to summon the magic of you pocket dimension and empower a creature you can see within the distance you can summon a creature to.

For one hour the hp of the empowered creature Doubles, it gains +2 Ac, all of its attacks are considered Magical, it gets resistance to non magical attacks, becomes one size bigger. and its stats become 1.5 rounded down.
This feature has two charges, each charge takes a full day to recover.
For each charge used the healing and ailment dispersion of the pocket dimension both get reduced in half, and you cant make new contracts until it recovers

Since you are connected the pocket dimension, as it exhausts its magic, you also get tired, your move speed is reduced by half, and you roll with disadvantage, you get one point of exaustion. If you use both charges, one hour after the 2nd charge is used you faint for 12 hours.

classFeature.name: Stamina

Your Brawler level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the stamina Points column of the Bralwer table.

You can spend these points to fuel various Stamina features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more Stamina features as you gain levels in this class.
Stamina Points are refreshed at the start and end of encounters.
Some of your Stamina features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Stamina save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Str/con/dex modifier

subclassFeature.name: Tiger style
entries: The Tiger Style embodies ferocity, power, and relentless aggression. Practitioners channel the spirit of the tiger — a predator that strikes fast and hard, overwhelming its prey with strength and precision. Movements are low, grounded, and explosive, emphasizing powerful strikes, crushing grips, and tearing motions meant to dominate the opponent.

In combat, the Tiger Style favors bravery and intimidation, meeting force with greater force. It relies on sharp, decisive attacks — claws, fists, or weapons — that aim to end a fight quickly. Defensively, it teaches resilience: to absorb blows like muscle and hide, then retaliate with primal fury.

entries: From level 2 Your unarmed attacks are complemented by the tiger Claw: Your unarmed strikes can be treated as claws. On hit, they deal slashing damage instead of bludgeoning.
Instead of the usual martial strikes damage, your martial strikes now deal 1d4+ your chosen modifier + your PB instead

entries: Starting at 10th level, you can move in sudden, swaying ways. You gain the following benefits:
Leap to Your Feet. When you're prone, you can stand up by spending 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed.

Redirect Attack. When a creature misses you with a melee attack roll, you can use your reaction to cause that attack to hit one creature of your choice, other than the attacker, that you can see within 5 feet of you, additionally if its a ranged attack you can also choose a creature up to 15 feet behind you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your PB+3.
You have +3 to all your STR and CON saving throws

You can choose to take a -5 penalty on attack roles, and if the attack hits you deal extra 12 damage or you can choose to take a +5 bonus on the attack roll and if the attack hits it deals less 10 damage. You can only take one, and you must declare it before rolling.

entries: From level 15 while you are below half your hit points, your unarmed strikes deal an additional 1d8 damage.
You have advantage on Grapple checks.

Once per short or long rest, when you reduce a creature to 0 HP with an unarmed strike, you can roar. All enemies within 30 ft must make a Wisdom saving throw(10+STR+PB) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
You gain proficiency in insight, if you are already proficient you gain a +2 to all insight checks instead.
If you use a simple weapon you deal extra 1d8+PB damage.
You have advantage on rolls made to track creatures.

subclassFeature.name: Tiger Apex
entries: At level 18 your unarmed strikes crit on a 18–20.
When you reduce a creature to 0 HP, you may immediately move up to half your speed and  make another unarmed strike against a creature within reach and you recover 10hp.
Grappled creatures automatically take 2d8 slashing damage at the start of your turn as your grip is sharp.
Your intimidation presence is legendary — creatures have disadvantage on saving throws against being frightened by you and you cant be frightened.

subclassFeature.name: SwarmKeeper
entries: Feeling a deep connection to the environment around them, some rangers reach out through their magical connection to the world and bond with a swarm of nature spirits. The swarm becomes a potent force in battle, as well as helpful company for the ranger. Some Swarmkeepers are outcasts or hermits, keeping to themselves and their attendant swarms rather than dealing with the discomfort of others. Other Swarmkeepers enjoy building vibrant communities that work for the mutual benefit of all those they consider part of their swarm.

subclassFeature.name: Gathered Swarm
entries: At 3rd level, a swarm of intangible nature spirits has bonded itself to you and can assist you in battle.
As a bonus Action you can summon a swarm to aid you You can only have one swarm at the time.

entries.name: When you summon a swarm you Choose which form the swarm takes
entries: Insects
Rats
Ravens
Spiders
Bats
BlueBees

entries.name: The swarm has its own stat block:
entries: Ability scores STR:3|DEX:14|CON:10|INT:3|WIS:4|CHAR:1 Raven:INT:6|WIS:7
Saving throws: DEX, CON
HP 3D8+6 or 19
AC 13
Speed: Insects,Rats,Spiders: 30ft walking| ravens,bats,bluebees: 30ft fly| spiders,insects 20ft climb
Senses: Insects,Bats>BlindSight 30ft |Spiders,Bluebees>blindsight 15ft
Resistances: Slashing,Piercing,Bludgeoning from non magic attacks.
Condition Immunities: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned
Skills: Raven: Perception
Traits Swarm | insects,spider: spider climb|  BlueBees: Smoke Weakness| Spider: web walker
Actions:
Insects: Bites: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (2d4 + 1) Poison damage.
Ravens:  Beaks. Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage.
Spiders:  Bites. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 6 (2d4+2) piercing damage plus 5 (1d8+1) poison damage.
Bats: Bites. Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (2d4+1) Piercing damage.

BlueBee: Sting. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 5 (2d4+1) piercing damage. The target must make a Constitution saving throw Equal to your spell save dc or take 10 (4d4) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If the poison damage reduces the target to 0 hit points, the target is stable, but remains unconscious, even after regaining hit points. An unconscious creature can be woken by taking an action to shake it awake, otherwise the creature will awaken in 8 hours.
Bonus Action:

Spider: Too Many Legs. The swarm mobs a creature in their space and attaches or detaches to them. When the swarm takes damage other than psychic damage, the attached creature also takes half as much damage. The attached creature has disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than the swarm, and attacks against the attached creature have advantage.

While attached, the swarm can't attack another target. The attached creature or     another creature who can reach them can shake off the swarm and detach them as an action. The swarm can detach by spending 5 feet of their movement.

Raven: Cacophony (Recharge 6). Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature in the swarm's space. Failure: The target has the Deafened condition until the start of the swarm's next turn. While Deafened, the target also has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

The Swarm obeys your commands as best as it can. It takes its turn on your initiative. On your turn, you can verbally command the beast where to move (no action required by you). You can use your action to verbally command it to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, or Help action. If you don’t issue a command, the Swarm takes the Dodge action. Once you have the Extra Attack feature, you can make one weapon attack yourself when you command the beast to take the Attack action. While traveling through your favored terrain with only the beast, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.

If you are incapacitated or absent, the beast acts on its own, focusing on protecting you and itself. The beast never requires your command to use its reaction, such as when making an opportunity attack.

If the Swarm dies or you dismiss it as a bonus action, you can obtain another one by spending 8 hours magically bonding with another beast that isn’t hostile to you, either the same type of beast as before or a different one.

entries.name: Once on each of your turns if the swarm is within 10 feet of you, you can cause the swarm to assist you in one of the following ways, immediately after you hit a creature with an attack:
entries: The swarm makes one attack against the attack's target.
The attack's target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be moved by the swarm up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice.
You are moved by the swarm 5 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice.
The Swarm Swarms a creature, making it harder for the creature to move outside of the swarm, when a creature is swarmed it must make a dc 8+your wis mod+your PB, or the swarm moves alongside them.

entries.name: After you reach level 7 in this class and again at 13th and 16th the swarm ability scores increase by 2.
entries: The swarm gains extra 2d8 Hp
The Swarm Ac increases by 2.
Each of the Swarms bites, beaks, stings gain extra 2d4 damage on the basic dmg, additionally the spider gains 1d8 poison damage and the bluebee gains 2d4 poison damage.
The swarm Gains 5ft of blindsight.
The swarm gains 5ft of walking/fly speed and climbing speed when applicable.

entries.name: At level 7 the swarm gains multiattack.
entries: The insects gain Avoidance.
The Rats gain Blood Frenzy.
The  Ravens gain Flyby and Keen senses.
The spiders gain Web Walker, Web Sense and Web Bolt.
The Bats gain Flame Essence(DC15, 4d4) its attacks deal extra 3d4 fire damage and it gains resistance to fire damage.
The BlueBees gain Corrosive form (3d8) and Aggressive.

subclassFeature.name: Swarmkeeper Magic
entries: Also at 3rd level, you learn the Mage Hand cantrip if you don't already know it. When you cast it, the hand takes the form of your swarming nature spirits.

You also learn an additional spell of 1st level or higher when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Swarmkeeper Spells table. Each spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.
3rd Faerie Fire, Mage Hand
5th Web, Flock of Familiars(free once a day)
9th Gaseous Form, Sending
13th Arcane Eye,Giant Insect
17th Insect Plague,Steel Wind Strike

subclassFeature.name: Writhing Tide
entries: Beginning at 7th level, you can condense part of your swarm into a focused mass that lifts you up. As a bonus action, you gain a flying speed of 15 feet and can hover. This effect lasts for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
The first time your swarm Creature created by gathered swarm attacks each combat, it dealts extra dmg equal to your wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Mighty Swarm
entries: At 11th level, your Gathered Swarm grows mightier in the following ways
If a creature fails its saving throw against being moved by the Gathered Swarm, you can also cause the swarm to knock the creature prone.
When you are moved by Gathered Swarm, it gives you half cover until the start of your next turn.
When a friendly creature is inside the swarm's space it gains half cover.
When a swarmed creature fails the saving throw and moves your swarm can make an attack agaisnt it

subclassFeature.name: Swarming Dispersal
entries: When you reach 15th level, you can discorporate into your swarm, avoiding danger. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to that damage before the damage takes effect(if you already have resistance you gain immunity instead), this lasts for 1 minute. You vanish into your swarm and then teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you, where you reappear with the swarm.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Master
entries: The Beast Master archetype embodies a friendship between the civilized races and the beasts of the world. United in focus, beast and ranger work as one to fight the monstrous foes that threaten civilization and the wilderness alike. Emulating the Beast Master archetype means committing yourself to this ideal, working in partnership with an animal as its companion and friend.

subclassFeature.name: Ranger's Companion
entries: At 3rd level, you gain a beast companion that accompanies you on your adventures and is trained to fight alongside you. Choose a beast that is no larger than Medium and that has a challenge rating of 1 or lower your ranger level. The beast's CR is always gonna be 1/3 of  your ranger level, when its time to up the Cr of your beast you use the monster upgrade page.

The beast obeys your commands as best as it can. It takes its turn on your initiative. On your turn, you can verbally command the beast to move, Attack, Dash, Disengage, or Help action. If you don't issue a command, the beast takes the Dodge action. Once you have the Extra Attack feature, you can make one weapon attack yourself when you command the beast to take the Attack action. While traveling through your favored terrain with only the beast, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.

If you are incapacitated or absent, the beast acts on its own, focusing on protecting you and itself. The beast never requires your command to use its reaction, such as when making an opportunity attack.
If the beast dies, you can obtain another one by spending 8 hours magically bonding with another beast that isn't hostile to you, either the same type of beast as before or a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Exceptional Training
entries: When you and your beast are within 5ft of a creature you and your beast get advantage on attack rolls against that creature.
You can cast spells with a range of touch from your beast. Additionally if you and your beast are in your favorite terrain and the spell lets you do an attack roll you have a +1 to the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Fury
entries: Starting at level 14th your beast can now Rage much like a barbarian.
You beast gains Advantage on Constitution skills and saving throws while raging.
While raging your beast gains 10 movement speed.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Sharing
entries: Beginning at 15th level, when you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your beast companion with the spell if the beast is within 60 feet of you. If you are on your favorite terrain the duration is 1.5 times.

Additionally when you and your beast are within 10ft of each other and when you or you beast are prompt to make a dexterity saving throw to take half damage, you instead take none on a success. If you are on your favorite terrain you have a +2 to the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Flames of War
entries: When you select this domain at 1st level, creatures you have made a contract with gain the power of the flames.
Your contracted creatures’ attacks deal 1 + PB fire damage.
At level 5 this increases to 2 + PB; at level 10 to 3 + PB; at level 15 to 4 + PB; and at level 18 to 5 + PB.
Your contracted creatures gain resistance to fire damage.
Your contracted creatures can shed bright light in a 10 ft. radius and dim light for an additional 10 ft.

Your contracted creatures can manifest a flame aura that sheds 5 ft. bright light and 5 ft. dim light. When your contracted creatures are hit by a melee attack, the attacker takes fire damage equal to 1 + PB (scaling as above).

subclassFeature.name: Blazing Strike
entries: From level 6 you and your contracted creatures gain the Dash action as a bonus action, leaving behind fiery sparks.
When they Dash, you can choose up to one creature within 5 ft. of their path to take damage equal to your Summoner level.
You learn the Produce Flame cantrip if you don’t already know it. Your contracted creatures also learn the cantrip as psionics which they can cast at will.

Your creatures gain the trait Blazing Strike: Once per long rest, you can empower one attack into a Blazing Strike. If the attack misses, the feature isn’t expended. If the attack hits, it deals an additional 2d8 fire damage and ignites the target (taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of its turns for 1 minute). The creature can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC starting on the 2nd turn to end the effect.

When you deal damage to a creature, you can expend hit dice to curse that creature. You roll the expended hit dice, dealing fire damage equal to the result to the target, but you take half that amount as damage.

subclassFeature.name: Inferno’s Call
entries: Starting at 14th level, your contracted creatures gain immunity to fire damage and you gain resistance to fire damage. If you already resist fire damage, you instead gain immunity.

You can choose 2 spells of 5th level or lower with the fire descriptor from the Sorcerer or Wizard list, and they count as Summoner spells for you. Your creatures learn the same spells as psionics that they can cast a number of times equal to half your proficiency modifier per day.

Whenever you cast a fire spell you can add your Charisma modifier to the damage. You can also cause your contracted creatures within 60 ft. of you to burst with flame, forcing creatures within 15 ft. of them to make a Dexterity saving throw or take fire damage equal to your Summoner level.
If you curse a creature with the effect of Blazing Strike, you know the location, distance, and direction of the cursed creature for 1 minute.

subclassFeature.name: Avatar of Flame
entries: At level 18 you and your contracted creatures can emit a 25 ft. aura of searing heat. Enemies of your choice that start their turn in this aura take 2d8 fire damage.
The light your creatures shed increases to 20 ft. bright and 20 ft. dim.
You can activate WorldFire Surge (1/long rest) unleashing a cataclysm of living flame for 5 rounds.

Initial Eruption: When activated, you and your contracted creatures each erupt into a burst of flames. Each enemy within 20 ft. must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = your Spell Save DC) or be blinded until the end of their next turn. On a success, they are not blinded.
Empowered Strikes: During the first turn, your attacks and your contracted creatures’ attacks deal maximum damage instead of rolling, and deal an additional +5 fire damage.

Tornado of Flame (Optional Trigger): If you and at least three contracted creatures are within 30 ft. of each other when you activate Worldfire Surge, you create a towering flame tornado for the first round. This tornado is 5 ft. around you and your creatures and 80 ft. tall. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the tornado takes 6d8 fire damage. The tornado provides half cover to you and your creatures but does not fully block vision.
Lingering Flamefield: Inside the flamefield, fire resistance is nullified, and fire immunity is reduced to resistance. Cold damage and attack rolls made with cold damage are halved.
You and your creatures gain resistance against cold damage, and you may automatically extinguish nonmagical flames within 30 ft. if you wish.

subclassFeature.name: Life Sharing
entries: When you Select this domain at 1st level Creature you have made a contract with gain max Hp equal to the healing tab on the domain tabble.
Creatures in The life domain additionally heal hp equal to your Summoner level + PB.
You gain Max hp equal to twice your PB

subclassFeature.name: Life Giving
entries: At 6th Level You gain a Hp pool equal to the healing tab on the summoning tabble + PB.
The Hp in this pool can be given to a creature within your summoning distance as a bonus action.
You and your contracted creatures automatically stay stable after reaching 0 hit points. If you ever have to make a death saving throw you automatically succeed
You can learn 1 cantrip and 1 spell from any spell list that is 4th level or lower itheyt counts as a Summoner spells for you.

subclassFeature.name: Life Blooming
entries: Starting at 14th level both you and your contracted creatures regenerate hp equal to your Summoner level, if a creature already has regeneration it regenerates more hp equal to your Summoner level.
Additionally your contracted creatures gain the max number on their hit die used for hp, gaining max hp.
You can learn 2 spells from the cleric or paladin spell list that are of 5th level or bellow, they Count as Summoner spells for you.

subclassFeature.name: Life Replanish
entries: At level 18 once per long rest you can recover mana points equal to your Summoner level.
You can Upcast spells to 6th level without risking destroying the dimension inside of you however to upcast from 5th level to 6th you must spend 5 mana points instead of the usual 1.
If you or your creatures dont have proficiency on constitution saving throw's, you and them gain it.
You and your creatures gain a +2 to your Constitution, additionally you and your contracted creatures make all Constitution saving throws at advantage.

subclassFeature.name: Martial ArtistT
entries: Martial Artist Brawlers are fighters who know martial arts in some way, be it by discovering a book somewhere, frequenting a dojo, or it runs on the familly.

subclassFeature.name: Tool proficiency
entries: Starting from lvl 1 when you choose this subclass you gain proficiency in Martial Weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Stance Proficiency
entries: Begining at lvl 3 you can use your bonus action to enter or change into a stance from the following.
When you move the stance ends.
If you take dmg you need to make a Str/Dex/Con saving throw dc 15 or be put out stance.

items: The dc changes to 10 at lvl 6.
The dc changes to 5 at lvl 11.
You dont need to do a saving throw starting from lvl 16 onwards.

entries.name: Bull stance
entries: While you are in this stance you get extra 10ft of movement for the turn, and you can also dash as a bonus action.

You can spend one stamina point to use your action to perform a charge at your enemies(you must run at least 15 feet for it to work), you dash towards you enemies, if they are any obstacles in the way you can perform a acrobatics/streght/athletics check to either jump over destroy or push away the obstacles in the way, the dc is decided by the dm, when you get within 5ft of an enemy you can perform at atk roll with a weapon or your fists, the roll gets +3 to hit and +3 to dmg.

items: From lvl 6 your charge is upgraded, and small obstacles as pushed out of the way (you dont do checks for stuff like ball bearing dmg from spikes or stuff).
From lvl 11 your charge is upgraded, and you gain 10ft movemnt instead of 5.
From lvl 16 your charge is upgraded, and you get +7 to hit and +7 to dmg.

entries.name: Tortoise stance
entries: During this stance you have +2 to ac and can make saving throws with advantage.

items: From lvl 6 your stance is upgraded, getting +4 instead of +2 to ac.
From lvl 11 your stance is upgraded, getting +7 instead of +4 to ac.
From lvl 16 your stance is upgraded, getting +10 instead of +7 to ac.

entries.name: Tiger Stance
entries: While you are in this stance your attacks have a +2 to hit.

items: From lvl 6 your stance is upgraded, getting +4 instead of +2 to hit.

From lvl 11 your stance becomes more solid making you capable of attacking sneaky foes,(this is for disengage action and similar) make an atk roll and if it beats the opponent acrobatics or athletics check you take the oportunity atk.
From lvl 16 your charge is upgraded, getting +8 instead of +4 to hit.

subclassFeature.name: Tool Mastery
entries: Starting from lvl 11 you get more familiar with your tools, you can spend a stamina point add double you pb to weapon or unarmed related rolls for the turn.

subclassFeature.name: Intuition
entries: From lvl 16 onwards you can sorta of feel your oponent movements, you can spend 4 stamina points to once per encounter attack an enemy with advantage once and make an enemy atk on yourself be at disavantage.

subclassFeature.name: Tavern Brawler
entries: Tavern Brawlers are fighters who started to fight in taverns, and keep going for tavern fights, they like it.
With your experience in tavern brawling you know how to graple someone, you get advantage when grapling and proficiency in athletics.
Aditionally you gain  proficiency with improvised attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: Beginning at 1st level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your STR or CON modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Tavern Environment
entries: At level 3 ,you know how to throw things at other people, you gain a new action which allows you to throw things at other people.
You roll a d20 + STR or DEX and your pb, the damage is the one from the dmg tabble.
You can spent stamina points to add +1 to hit and 1d6 to the dmg per stamina point spent(max3).
You can use a bonus action instead but the dmg is cut in half.
Aditionally you also know how move around places full of obstacles, you get +5ft move speed

items: From lvl 6 you ignore difficult terrain and you get 10ft of movement instead of 5ft.
From lvl 11 you ignore small objects in the floor as you move such as ball bearing, spikes,wire traps etc. and you get 15ft of movement instead of 10ft.
From lvl 16 you get +20ft of movement instead of 15ft and you can dash as a bonus action .

subclassFeature.name: Scary Face
entries: begining at lvl 6 you are so terrifying that you can attempt to intimidate enemies mid combat as an action without disavatage (intimidation vs wis save).
You can spend a stamina point to add a +2 to the roll, and if you succeed the enemy is Frightened for 3 rounds, if they take dmg the effect ends.
You have advantage against being intimidated
You get proficiency in Intimidation.

subclassFeature.name: Battle Royal Experience
entries: Starting at lvl 11 after you hit someone you can spend 2 stamina points to take an attack action at an enemy within 5ft distance.
when you are being targeted by more than one enemy you get +2 ac, and after you reach lvl 16 you get +3ac instead.

subclassFeature.name: On the Nape
entries: By lvl 16 you are sure how make someone faint, you can spend 10 stamina points and perfom a special atk, you roll a 20 + either str, dex or con and pb, it does 1d20+pb dmg.
if you hit from behind you can roll another d20+pb for dmg and the enemy does a con save if they fail to beat your atk roll they fall unconcious for 1hour.

subclassFeature.name: Hydric Bloodline
entries: Your innate magic comes from draconic magic, not unlike those with the draconic bloodline, but rather than using the blood or essence of a dragon either you or your ancestors were given the powers of the hydra. Maybe an ancestor of yours entered a pact with an evil dragon but was tricked by the exact wording of the contract, and rather than give them draconic powers the dragon gave your ancestor hydra powers. Or maybe you underwent a unique and powerful ritual to try to become a dragon, not knowing the scales you had collected were not from a dragon. However you came to possess this rare form of natural magic, it is now yours to command.

subclassFeature.name: Hydric Spells
entries: At 1st level, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, slashing, poison or Bludgeoning. The chosen damage type is your elemental affinity, a natural part of the world that you can more easily create and control with your spells. aditionally choose another at Level 3

Choose one evocation spell of a level for which you have spell slots from either the sorcerer's or wizard's spell list that deals damage of the same type as your elemental affinity. You learn that spell, it doesn't count against the number of spells you can know, and if it was from the wizard's spell list it counts as a sorcerer spell for you. If the chosen spell lets you choose which type of damage it deals when you cast it, you must choose the same type of damage as one of your elemental affinities. If the spell would normally deal damage of a random type, it instead deals damage of a random type matching one of your elemental affinities. You learn another additional spell in this manner at 6th level, and again at 14th level and 18th level.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Heads
entries: Also at 1st level, you are capable of manifesting certain aspects of the hydra, changed by the elemental power of dragons. As a bonus action on your turn, you can magically summon a spectral hydra head, originating from your neck. You choose on which side of your head the hydra head sits. When you summon the head, choose one of your elemental affinities. The head takes on an appearance appropriate to the affinity selected, such as glowing red or wreathed in flames for fire, or glowing yellow-green with smoke pouring from its mouth for poison.

The head has an AC of 13 + your Dexterity modifier and hit points equal to twice your sorcerer level, immunity to its elemental affinity damage type, and it automatically succeeds on all saving throws. It disappears after one hour, if it drops to 0 hit points, or if you dismiss it as a bonus action. The maximum number of heads you can have summoned at once is equal to your sorcerer level divided by 2, rounded up, and you can dismiss multiple heads with the same bonus action.

Immediately after summoning the head, and on subsequent turns as a bonus action, you can make one melee weapon attack with the head, using your Charisma for the attack and damage rolls. You are proficient with this attack. It has a reach of 5 feet, and a target takes 1d4 damage of the head's elemental affinity if the attack hits. If you have more than one head, each one can make a separate attack with the same bonus action. The damage increases to 1d6 and the reach increases to 10 feet at 6th level, to 1d8 and 15 feet at 14th level, and to 1d10 and 20 feet at 18th level.

You can use an action to make each head you have breath their element in a 10ft cone dealing 2d6 their element damage on a failed  dexterity saving throw or half has much on a sucess, this action has Recharch 5-6. The damage and reach changes to 2d8 and 15ft at lvl 6th, 2d10 and 20ft at lvl 14th and to 2d10+ your charima modifier and 25ft at lvl 18. Recharge changes to 6 at level 18th

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution and Charisma modifier + PB (minimum of 1), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Short  or roll Initiative. If you have no uses of this feature remaining and you have sorcery points, you can spend 1 sorcery point to use this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Hydric Regeneration
entries: At 6th level, the hydra blood enhances your regenerative capacities. Whenever one of your hydra heads disappears, you regain hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1). This increases to twice your Constitution modifier (minimum of 2) at 14th level.
In addition, you choose a Third elemental affinity, allowing you to learn a wider variety of spells using your Hydric Spells feature.

subclassFeature.name: Hydra's Song
entries: Starting at 14th level, the hydra heads you summon become capable of casting spells as well using their own power. While you have a head summoned, you can use your bonus action to have the head cast a 1st-level evocation sorcerer spell you know with a casting time of 1 action without using any material components, with the head fulfilling any verbal and somatic components of the spell instead of you. The spell must deal damage of the same type as the head's elemental affinity, and it cannot require concentration. The head then shrivels and disappears.

If you have more than one head of the same affinity summoned, you can have additional heads contribute towards the casting of the spell. Each additional head sacrificed in this manner either increases the level the spell is cast at by 1 (as if casting a 1st-level spell from a spell slot of a higher level) or increases the level of spell the chosen spell can be by 1 (casting a 2nd-level or higher evocation spell instead of a 1st-level spell.) The spell originates from only one of the heads, and each head used in this way shrivels and disappears after the spell is cast.
In addition, you choose a Fourth elemental affinity, allowing you to learn a wider variety of spells using your Hydric Spells feature.

subclassFeature.name: Hydra Affinity
entries: At 18th level, the draconic magics of your hydric infusion fully manifest. You choose a Fifth elemental affinity, and then one damage type from the following: force, psychic, necrotic, radiant, or thunder. That becomes your Sixt elemental affinity, and you learn one spell from any spell list that deals that type of damage. This spell doesn't count against the number of spells you know, and follows the same damage restrictions as the spells you learned with your other elemental affinities. In addition, any time you would regain one or more hit points, you regain an additional 2 hit points.

subclassFeature.name: Sleeper Sorcerer
entries: Sleepers are sorcerers but the amount of magic they get when they awaken their powers is larger than most.
The magic inside you is strong, you cant really pinpoint where it comes from, but one thing you know, you cant handle very well, the power is so strong that makes you drowsy and sleepy.
While you are asleep your magic is mostly dormant, but when you are awake you need to constantly control your magic to keep it under control.
Rarely you are fully awake, as you level up you start to control this energy better, doing so lets you be awake for longer.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Cloud
entries: Your enormous magic causes you to be asleep, unconsciously you create a  cloud like object to help you sleep better, this cloud is thick enough for you to ride it. Its also very comfortable allowing you to fall asleep at any time, if other people would try to get in the cloud they have to pass a dc 15 arcana check or they pass through the cloud instead.

You can summon this cloud by using an action, the cloud appears in a space within 5 feet of you, of your choice, there can only be one cloud summoned at the same time, if you attempt to summon another cloud the previous one dispersers.

The cloud is medium, it has twice your hp, Its ac is 10+ your charisma modifier + pb,  its immune to non magical dmg. The cloud levitates 2ft from the ground ignoring terrain, it has 30ft of movement.

items: Having this cloud out gives you a sense of relief as it takes part of your magical energy
The cloud can have various colours and shapes you decide.

entries: The cloud has the same initiative as you, and acts on your turn.
The cloud is an extension of you, it can take the dash, dodge and disengage action, you can control it using your thoughts, additionally you can issue simple commands to the cloud.

items: From lvl 2 onwards sleeping on this cloud restores 1d6 hp and 1 sorcery point per hour.
From lvl 6 you learn to control you magic better the cloud now also has 15ft of flying speed. Additionally you cant be knocked out of the cloud against your will.

From lvl 14 onwards your control over the cloud is remarkable the cloud now has 30ft of flying speed, and it can transverse terrain much easier, no bumps or holes can affect it,(you can for example transverse the rough ocean on it no problems, except you will get wet).

subclassFeature.name: Out of control
entries: When you lose control of your magic either by being forcibly awake or other means your magic really gets out of control.

Within 10 feet, centered around you appears a magical storm, anything aside from you and your cloud that enters the storm is dealt randomly 1d8 cold, fire, lightning, Thunder, Radiant or  Force dmg per  2 sleeper level.
If you attempt to cast magic in this state your magic is empowered dealing more damage and becoming more difficult to avoid.

items: Your spells deal extra 1d6  equal half your sleeper level rounded up.
Your spell save dc is increased by half you sleeper lvl rounded up.
Your spells have +1 feet of range per sleeper level.

entries: Every time you cast a spell roll a d100 + you wisdom modifier, if the result is 50 or less the spell malfunctions and explodes, all creatures within 5 feet of the explosion take 2d6 dmg per spell level(same dmg type as the spell), any creature that took that damage must make a dexterity saving throw against your spell save dc or be moved 15 feet away from you per spell level. Creatures hitting something while being moved take 1d6 bludeonign damage per spell level

items: If the spell doesn't do dmg, the dmg type is becomes force dmg.

entries: These effects last  until you regain control of your magic, you must spend at least five minute while trying to regain control.

subclassFeature.name: Magic burst
entries: At 3rd level, you learn a better version of the metamagic empowered spell called magic burst, this is a different metamagic from empowered spell.

When you cast a spell you can spend 1 sorcery point + 1 sorcery point per spell level to roll 2x the dmg dice said on the spell, if the dmg rolls are bellow half the dice maximum number, they become half instead, additionally the spell effects are doubled in strength, things such as duration and range double .

items: If the spell has a spell save dc you can add twice your charisma modifier instead of just one time.

subclassFeature.name: Sleep Walking
entries: From 3rd level on your magical senses are strong enough that they even work while you are sleeping. While you are sleeping you gain some consciousness.
While you are asleep you can cast spells and perform simple actions. you cannot do or think complex things.

You still have your memory and you can access it, but its fuzzy, fuzzy in a way that if a enemy  resembles an ally, you block for a second, in this case you might think they are both your ally because its the strongest memory or the one that you have the most, if you have a deep grudge with the enemy and think about it daily it might be that one the strongest, making you think they are both the enemy.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Explosion
entries: Starting from lvl 6 When a creature gets within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to cause a magical explosion on that creature, the creature must make a dexterity saving throw on you spell dc or take 1d8 fire dmg equal to half your sleeper lvl rounded up, and be pushed back 2feet per sleeper level.
If the creature collides with something it will take 1d4 bludgeoning per 5ft traveled if the creature is reduced to half or lower of its hitpoints it is knocked prone.

subclassFeature.name: Magic protection
entries: From level 14 you can integrate your magic within you.

items: You gain bonus ac based on your charisma modifier.
You gain an aditional bonus equal to your charisma modifier on dice rolls related to magic.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Expertise
entries: At level 18 your proficiency with this magic that appeared on you is higher than ever, you gain expertise with arcana if you dont already have it.

Additionally when a creature makes a dice roll related to magic(including yourself), you can make that create re-roll it. You have a number of uses of this ability equal to your charisma modifier per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Sea Sorcerer
entries: The power of water is the strength of flexibility, resilience, and a relentless nature. Water parts to allow a ship to sail over it or a diver to plunge into it, but their passing leaves no mark. Water flowing down a mountain reaches the sea. It might bend and turn across valleys and down hillsides, but it slowly and steadily returns to the waves. Those whose souls are touched by the power of elemental water command a similar power.

Your heritage ties to powerful creatures of the sea, such as nereids, the lords of the merfolk, and elemental powers. Like a river, you feel the call of the ocean. The call is ever present in your heart, and you are never completely at peace until you are near the sea.

subclassFeature.name: Soul of the Sea
entries: At 1st level, your tie to the sea grants you the ability to breathe underwater, and you have a swim speed equal to your walking speed.

subclassFeature.name: Curse of the Sea
entries: When you choose this origin at 1st level, you learn the secret of infusing your spells with a watery curse.

When you hit a creature with a cantrip’s attack or when a creature fails a saving throw against your cantrip, you can curse the target until the end of your next turn or until you curse a different creature with this feature.

Once per turn when you cast a spell, you can trigger the curse if that spell deals cold or lightning damage to the cursed target or forces it to move. Doing so subjects the target to the appropriate additional effect below, and then the curse ends if the spell isn’t a cantrip (you choose the effect to use if more than one effect applies):

items: Cold Damage. If the affected target takes cold damage from your spell, the target’s speed is also reduced by 15 feet until the end of your next turn. If the spell already reduces the target’s speed, use whichever reduction is greater.
Lightning Damage. If the affected target takes lightning damage from your spell, the target takes additional lightning damage equal to your Charisma modifier.
Forced Movement. If the target is moved by your spell, increase the distance it is moved by 15 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Watery Defense
entries: At 6th level, you gain resistance to fire damage.

You also gain the ability to defend yourself by momentarily assuming a watery form. As a reaction when you are hit by an attack and take bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage from it, you can reduce that damage by an amount equal to your sorcerer level plus your Charisma score, and then you can move up to 30 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. Once you use this special reaction, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Shifting Form
entries: Starting at 14th level, you gain the ability to enter a liquid state while moving.
When you move on your turn, you take only half damage from opportunity attacks, and you can move through any enemy’s space but can’t willingly end your move there.

On your turn, you can move through any space that is at least 3 inches in diameter and do so without squeezing. When you stop moving, the regular squeezing rules apply if you’re in a space one size smaller than you. You can’t willingly stop in a space smaller than that, and if you’re forced to do so, you immediately flow to the nearest space that can fit you, back along the path of your movement.

subclassFeature.name: Water Soul
entries: Starting at 18th level, your being is altered by the power of the sea. You gain the following benefits:

items: You no longer need to eat, drink, or sleep.
A critical hit against you becomes a normal hit
You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Lore Mastery
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you become a compendium of knowledge on a vast array of topics. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses the Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion skill if you are proficient in that skill.

In addition, your analytical abilities are so well-honed that your initiative in combat can be driven by mental agility, rather than physical agility. When you roll initiative, it is either an Intelligence check or a Dexterity check for you (your choice).

subclassFeature.name: Spell Secrets
entries: At 2nd level, you master the first in a series of arcane secrets uncovered by your extensive studies.

When you cast a spell with a spell slot and the spell deals acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, radiant, or thunder damage, you can substitute that damage type with one other type from that list (you can change only one damage type per casting of a spell). You replace one energy type for another by altering the spell's formula as you cast it.

When you cast a spell with a spell slot and the spell requires a saving throw, you can change the saving throw from one ability score to another of your choice. Once you change a saving throw in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Altering Spells
entries: While the Spell Secrets feature offers increased versatility, at the table its effects can be difficult to spot by the other players. If you're playing a savant, take a moment to describe how you alter your spells. Think of a signature change your character is particularly proud of. Be inventive, and make the game more fun for everyone by playing up the sudden, unexpected tricks your character can employ. For example, a fireball transformed to require a Strength save might become a sphere of burning rock that shatters and slams into its target. A charm person that requires a Constitution save might take the form of a vaporous narcotic that alters the target's mood.

subclassFeature.name: Alchemical Casting
entries: At 6th level, you learn to augment spells in a variety of ways. When you cast a spell with a spell slot, you can expend one additional spell slot to augment its effects for this casting, mixing the raw stuff of magic into your spell to amplify it. The effect depends on the spell slot you expend.

An additional 1st-level spell slot can increase the spell's raw force. If you roll damage for the spell when you cast it, increase the damage against every target by 2d10 force damage. If the spell can deal damage on more than one turn, it deals this extra force damage only on the turn you cast the spell.
An additional 2nd-level spell slot can increase the spell's range. If the spell's range is at least 30 feet, it becomes 1 mile.
An additional 3rd-level spell slot can increase the spell's potency. Increase the spell's save DC by 2.

subclassFeature.name: Prodigious Memory
entries: At 10th level, you have attained a greater mastery of spell preparation. As a bonus action, you can replace one spell you have prepared with another spell from your spellbook. You can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Magic
entries: At 14th level, your knowledge of magic allows you to duplicate almost any spell. As a bonus action, you can call to mind the ability to cast one spell of your choice from any class's spell list. The spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, you mustn't have it prepared, and you follow the normal rules for casting it, including expending a spell slot. If the spell isn't a wizard spell, it counts as a wizard spell when you cast it. The ability to cast the spell vanishes from your mind when you cast it or when the current turn ends.
You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
